newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon government sees private 1996 wheat imports.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon government sees private 1996 wheat imports.

text.p: The Lebanese government does not plan further purchases of wheat on the international markets this year but it expects the private sector to import additional supplies, an Economy Ministry official said on Tuesday.

"We have about 80,000 tonnes in storage and we have bought 16,000 tonnes of local wheat from farmers, so I think this will be enough for the next three months," the official at the Office of Cereals and Sugar Beet told Reuters.

The office is part of the economy ministry, which this year has made purchases of 200,000 tonnes of wheat through local agents of international companies -- half of Lebanon's yearly requirements of 400,000 tonnes.
The official said the private sector -- which usually buys the other half of the country's wheat needs -- has so far bought 75,000 tonnes this year and will probably make more purchases this year.
This left the theoretical possibility of private sector imports of a further 125,000 tonnes, but the official said it was not clear how much the sector would in fact import.

"I think the private sector will make more tenders for wheat but I don't know for how much exactly as the consumption may differ from last year," the official said, adding that he had no news of planned tenders by the private sector.
